subcategory: autonomous driving: regulation retrieval + LLM reasoning agent
task: Action-level traffic-rule compliance and safety assessment for autonomous vehicles
problem: Traffic regulations are complex, context-dependent and region-specific; rule-based systems and LLMs relying on pre-trained knowledge miss local rules or hallucinate them.
architecture: DriveReg: a VLM performs chain-of-thought environment analysis of multi-view images and generates a retrieval query; a Traffic Regulation Retrieval agent fetches rules from regional regulation documents (FAISS, top-5); an LLM reasoning agent assesses each candidate action for compliance and safety with CoT.
retriever: text-embedding-ada-002 and paraphrase-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings with FAISS similarity search (K = 5)
generator: GPT-4o (reasoning agent); VLM for scene analysis
knowledge_source: traffic regulation documents and safety guidelines of Boston, Singapore and Los Angeles

datasets.name: DriveReg Scenarios Dataset
datasets.details: 500 hypothesized and real-world driving scenarios from Boston, Singapore and Los Angeles, labelled for compliance and safety

key_results: Hypothesized normal scenarios: 98% compliance and 98% safety accuracy; hard scenarios: 99% compliance and 94% safety.
On hard cases compliance improves from 86% (GPT-4o) to 99% with retrieval and the reasoning agent.
Regulation retrieval accuracy on 20 Boston-hard scenarios (top-5): 1.00 vs 0.60 for BM25.
Detailed reasoning takes about 2 seconds per decision with GPT-4o.
strengths: Region-specific rule grounding with interpretable reasoning; includes a real-vehicle deployment test.
New benchmark annotated at the action level across three cities; results over 5 random seeds.

limitations.text: Some failures come from perception errors, e.g. misidentifying solid lane markings as broken.
The action space is a small predefined set of high-level manoeuvres; retrieval comparison uses only 20 scenarios.

notes: Real-world test with a human driver in control, system running in parallel.
title: Driving with Regulation: Trustworthy and Interpretable Decision-Making for Autonomous Driving with Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning
